picks.title: DeepSeek deep-sixed at all US federal civilian agencies
picks.excerpt: DHS on Monday ordered federal civilian agencies to stop using and remove all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, including third-party services developed using DeepSeek; the order's scope is broad and vague. (Yonhap reports China called it politicisation of science and technology.)
picks.rationale: A concrete federal order: DHS directs all civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek and DeepSeek-derived third-party services, which reaches vendors who build on DeepSeek weights. It is a new decision, separate from the 09-30 superintelligence EO. Attribute the 'broad and vague' reading to The Register and the 'politicisation' reaction to China via Yonhap.

picks.title: Democrats warn tech firms of election security 'backsliding' ahead of midterms
picks.excerpt: Senior congressional Democrats on intelligence and election oversight sent a letter to 25 companies including Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and TikTok, warning that inaccurate AI-generated voting information and weakened safeguards could expose voters to manipulation before Nov 3.
picks.rationale: An official congressional letter to 25 named AI and platform companies about AI-generated voting misinformation ahead of Nov 3. It is a new action, not the 10-19 Wesleyan ad-spend data. Keep the framing neutral: say what the letter asks and who sent it, and attribute the 'backsliding' claim to the senders.

picks.title: UK finance watchdog wants firms to report AI failures and close calls
picks.excerpt: FCA chief data officer Jessica Rusu said firms' incident reporting must cover significant AI failures and near-misses as increasingly autonomous agents enter financial services, demanding clear accountability. (Primary: FCA speech 'Building the future of finance in the age of AI'.)
picks.rationale: Swap-in for the Ars Meta torrenting order, which books is publishing today. The UK's financial regulator has officially stated that firms' incident reporting must cover AI failures and near-misses involving autonomous agents. AI is central to the story, it comes from a primary FCA source, and it changes what UK fintech builders have to log. The copy must call it a supervisory expectation set out in a speech, not a new rule. It is a new jurisdiction, distinct from the 10-09 MAS and 10-11 US incident-reporting cards.

picks.title: NYC proposes crackdown on AI customer service chatbots
picks.excerpt: Mamdani administration proposed a first-of-its-kind city rule requiring businesses to give customers a quick off-ramp to a human agent when an AI chatbot can't resolve their request. (Off-list; no allowed outlet covered it.)
picks.rationale: A proposed municipal rule that directly changes how businesses deploy AI chatbots, because it requires a human off-ramp. That makes it the most actionable item of the day for builders. The domain is off-list (an exception because no allowed outlet covered it). The copy must call it a proposed rule, not an adopted one.

picks.title: S. Korea's U.N. envoy named co-chair of global AI governance dialogue
picks.excerpt: UNGA President appointed Korean Ambassador Cha Ji-hoon and Saint Kitts and Nevis' Mutryce Agatha Williams to co-chair preparations for the 2027 UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (May 3-4, 2027).
picks.rationale: An official UNGA appointment that sets who steers the 2027 UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (May 3-4, 2027). It brings in a multilateral governance angle and is distinct from the 09-21 Global Digital Compact review commentary.
